# Short answer

Telltale's two matters use similar approaches, but both are Telltale-specific client instructions. Toil & Trouble hasn't given any comparable instructions, so I'd propose them to Mr. Oyelaran rather than assume them.

## How Telltale wants expert reports reviewed

The approach is the same in Hartwell and Delmore. Telltale's regulatory affairs group (Odalys Fennimore) must compare every defense expert report with Telltale's regulatory submissions for inconsistencies before it is served.

- **Hartwell:** The group needs ten business days. Reports can't be shared outside the firm and the expert until cleared. Comments go through counsel and are logged, so the exchange stays protected as work done at counsel's direction. The firm asked Dr. Vandermeer for a near-final draft by January 30, 2026, ahead of the March 17 deadline. It also planned to confirm that the drafts stipulation with plaintiff's counsel covers the process.
- **Delmore:** The group gets two weeks. Comments are routed through counsel to the expert, never directly. Dr. Ouellette's draft was requested by September 26, 2025, ahead of the October 31 deadline. Any second expert, such as Dr. Marchetti, goes through the same review.
- **Engaging experts:** Telltale wants to be consulted first. Hartwell requires three names per discipline with prior testimony notes. Delmore requires General Counsel discussion and fee quotes before any testifying expert is signed.

## When Telltale will talk settlement

- **Hartwell:** No offer and no engagement on figures until the treating cardiologist, Dr. Teague, is deposed and the transcript is read. The firm then sends General Counsel an assessment and recommended range for the claims committee. Authority above $500,000 needs CFO sign-off. The firm recommended declining mediation until after the deposition, then proposing it in January 2026 if the transcript is favorable.
- **Delmore:** Listen if plaintiff raises resolution, but give no number and make no offer until the treating cardiologist's deposition. The firm will attend mediation to listen and put no number on the table unless Dr. Pratt's testimony helps. The client must approve the mediator and confirm confidentiality first.

I have left out the restricted settlement information in the Delmore file, which is limited to that case team. It shouldn't inform another client's matter.

## Adapting this for Toil & Trouble

- **Expert review:** The file shows no requirement for a pre-service review. I'd ask Mr. Oyelaran whether he wants one, for example a check of expert reports against the safety-listing submissions. If so, copy the mechanics: counsel-routed comments, a log, a fixed review window, and a draft deadline set before the October 2 designation date.
- **Settlement timing:** Toil & Trouble's sequence is different. It wants mediation early, before any expert is disclosed. The firm has no authority, and no offer may be made in any form without Mr. Oyelaran's written approval. The Telltale trigger (wait for a deposition) doesn't carry over. Our trigger is the inspection result, the document exchange, and preliminary mediation authority.
- **Dates:** Today is November 3, 2026, so the July 17 mediation deadline and the August 21 and October 2 designation dates have passed. The file doesn't show whether mediation occurred or the case settled. Please confirm the current status before applying any of this.
